title: Functional Equation f(x+y) = f(x)f(y)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Suppose f satisfies f(x + y) = f(x) f(y) for all real x and y, and f(1) = 3. Determine f(0), justifying why the zero solution is excluded, and compute f(2).

steps.title: Probe the Equation at the Origin
steps.explanation: Setting x = y = 0 turns the equation into f(0) = f(0)^2, whose only real solutions are 0 and 1 after factoring t(t - 1) = 0.
steps.why: A number equal to its own square must be 0 or 1; the functional equation collapses to this algebraic test at the origin.

steps.title: Eliminate the Degenerate Branch
steps.explanation: If f(0) were 0, then pairing any x with 0 would force f(x) = f(x) * 0 = 0, making f identically zero and contradicting f(1) = 3.
steps.why: The hypothesis f(1) = 3 selects the nonzero solution branch, so f(0) = 0 is inconsistent with the given data.

steps.title: Conclude f(0) = 1
steps.explanation: With the zero branch refuted, the only remaining candidate is f(0) = 1, mirroring the empty-exponent law a^0 = 1 for the exponential-type solutions this equation describes.
steps.why: A proof by cases closes when exactly one case survives the contradiction, leaving 1 as the forced value.

steps.title: Build f(2) from f(1)
steps.explanation: Choosing x = y = 1 splits 2 into 1 + 1, and the product rule converts the sum into a square of f(1).
steps.why: The equation converts addition in the input into multiplication in the output, which is the defining behavior of an exponential function.
